DE FRANCESCHI , a family originally from Friuli (Italian: Friuli) in northeastern Italy, from where several of its branches migrated to Istria in the 17th century and settled in Gologorica near Pazin. In their homeland, they belonged to a circle of small feudal lords in the service of the patriarch of Aquileia, and have been mentioned since the 15th century. In the 16th century, they lived in the settlement of Villa di Mione, not far from the castle of Argonsa in Cárnia, from where they migrated to Istria. The family surname is recorded in documents in the forms De Franceschi (17th century and later sources), Defranceschi (later sources), and in the 20th century also de Franceschi. The first form was most often used, which family members also consider to be the original. The first mention of the family in the civil registers of Gologorica dates back to 1661, when the craftsman (mistro) Zuanne was recorded as the godfather. The De Franceschi family moved to Istria as merchants and craftsmen, and in their new homeland some branches acquired considerable wealth and a prominent social position, investing money in the purchase of arable land and other real estate, and engaging in farming and livestock breeding. In Gologorica, they already owned a large stone house in 1701, which for a long time was a social and cultural center from which the influence of Italian culture spread to members of the Croatian cultural circle in the area. The family's financial position enabled its members to study. Thus, Sebastian and his son Gian Battista were notaries in Buzet and Cárnia in the period 1688–1782. The doctor Francesco completed his medical studies in Padua (1693) and served in Istria (including Motovun) and Cárnia. The surgeon Cosma Damiani also graduated in medicine in Padua (1710). In In 1712, the prefect of Gologorica, Gian Battista, was on the side of the serfs who rebelled against the violence of the governor Gaetano Marotti and was therefore imprisoned in the tower of the Pazin castle, from where he was rescued by the then Gologorica feudal lord from the Turinetti family, the Marquise de Prie. Gian Battista's son Gian Pier became a tax collector in the service of the owner of the Gologorica fief, CA Biotz, in the mid-18th century. Since 1772, Gian Piero's son Giuseppe has been a tax tenant in that area and in Novaki, and his second son Gian Matteo was a parish priest in Gologorica in the 1740s, then a cathedral canon in Pićan and an apostolic protonotary. Officer Gian Battista, son of Gian Battista, fought as a lieutenant in the Seven Years' War of 1756–63, and was also the commander of the Bribir castle (until 1771). At the beginning of the 19th century, among several family branches, the one to which Giacomo and Giuseppe belong stands out(died 1838), sons of Giuseppe. They significantly expanded and rounded out their family's estates (often by seizing debtors' estates). Like their ancestors, they valued only Italian culture and language. In political terms, they were pro-Austrian. Giacomo participated in the rebellion against the French in Istria as early as 1809, and after the establishment of Austrian rule in Istria (1813), he was a member of the delegation to the Austrian Emperor Francis I with the Pićan canon A. Tesacko; during the emperor's visit to Istria in 1816, both brothers accompanied him. In the subsequent period, Giuseppe's descendants stood out, acting politically in line with the awakening of the Italian national movement, especially his son, politician and historian → CARLO . Carlo's son → CAMILLO was also a historian, and his second son → GIULIO was a painter. The third, Gian Pietro (1854–1884), studied law in Graz and was one of the founders and president of the Società degli studenti italiani there, and after completing his studies he became a judge in Rovinj and Pula (from 1880). His interest in other scientific fields is reflected in his contributions on literature, Istrian antiquities and biographical studie

De Franceschi, Carlo , lawyer, notary and historian-medievalist (Trieste, 11.IX.1900 - Venice, 30.IV.1972). He is the son of Camille and the grandson of Carl, in Mlet. and in July historiography called also Carlo junior. He finished high school in Trieste, and studied at the Faculty of Law in Padua, then opened a notary office in Rovinj. There he married Caterina Bembo (from the family of the Istrian nobile, owner of the Bale castle). After the events of October 1943, when his brother-in-law was among the victims thrown into the pit (foib), he took refuge with his family in Venice, got a notary position and settled with his father, Camilla, in the Soranzo Palace.

The De Franceschi family owned the castle of Agrons near the river Degano, to the south. part of the Gorto Valley, in Carnia. Documents from 1467 and 1471 testify to the investment that Leonardus Francisci received from the governor of Friuli with the obligation to perform military service. A document from 1502 mentions Sir Leonardus Christoforus Francisci quondam Johannis gismanus de Carnia, while the archival sources at the end of the first half. XVI century record some de Franciscus in the village of Mioneu, above Ovar, not far from the castle of Agrons. Camillo De F. assumes that this is the Carnian-Friulian branch of the genus De F. that settled in Gologorica, probably in a migratory wave.

lines.n: Franceschi dalle Rose Move 1040 to Venice
lines.note: a branch of the family (Franceschi dalle Rose) moved to Venice in 1040 and settled in the Giudeca region - a monastery was later built there ... 'monasterio delle convertite ... 'where family members are buried.

Niccolo´ received from the Croatian-Hungarian King Louis I the Great of Anjou for the merits of the estate in Zadar and its surroundings, and according to the charter signed in Buda on March 8, 1359 (according to some sources 1369) he was admitted to the royal hereditary Hungarian-Croatian nobility and received coat of arms. Since then, the genealogy of the family can be traced on the territory of Croatia, so Niccolo, according to the data known to this day, is taken as the earliest ancestor of the family - its ancestor. Along with him, in the service of the Anjouans, the praises of Francesco (1342–1400) and Steffano (1394–1438) are mentioned, ‘nobile cavaliere e consigliere’. The family today does not have copies of the charter. In Zadar, the Franceschi are associated with the noble families of Vallay, Camozzini, Grisogono, and its members performed various civilian and military duties in the city in the service of the Venetian Republic.

In the 18th century, Toma , a notary public, distinguished himself in Zadar . He was admitted to the Zadar City Council by inheritance law and took the oath in 1714. He was appointed notary public in 1722. He worked for a full forty years, and he also ran his office in the "Illyrian" - Croatian language. His son Ivan Krševan also acted as a notary public. In 1838, the family sought confirmation of the nobility from the Austrian commission, enclosing abundant documentation and genealogy, and was included in the Collection of Dalmatian Nobility (Heyer, 1873).

lines.n: Francesca de Franceschi 1500s venice to Omis
lines.note: In the second half of the 16th century, Francesca de Franceschi (1520–1598) sent Venice to Omis as a member of the city senate and is mentioned in parish books. Since then, two branches of the family have been developing in parallel, in Zadar and Omiš, which have nurtured mutual ties for centuries.

lines.n: Giovanni (Zuane) de Franceschi led a siege against the Turks
lines.note: Giovanni (Zuane) de Franceschi (1673–1741), governatore, is particularly prominent in the war between the Venetian Republic and Turkey in 1718, in which he led local volunteers from Pisak through Vrulja to the siege of Imotski. In Pisak, in the local church in front of the altar, there is an old family tomb on which the family coat of arms is carved. After three days, these volunteers were joined in the siege by an army of 200 German and 200 Swiss mercenaries with cannons, and the same number of cavalry from Sinj. In the action, Imotski and Vrgorac were liberated, and the border between Dalmatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina was determined, which has remained to this day. For her merits, Zuana de Franceschi received from the Venetian Republic the estates of Archbishop Čaušević - land, houses, a mill, a tower on the river Vrljica in the area called Perinuša. This venture was sung by Andrija Kačić-Miošič in his songbook ' A pleasant conversation of the people of Slovenia ', in which he mentions Ivan Perinović, who for his merits receives the estates of Archbishop Čaušević. These estates are still partly owned by the Franceschi family.
